news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Announces Oral Presentation of LX2006 at the International Congress of Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders 2026 (MDS)
news.summary: Dr. Theresa Zesiewicz will give an oral presentation on Oct 7 (12:30 KST, Seoul) with new mFARS subscore analyses showing neurologic improvements in LX2006-treated Friedreich ataxia patients, complementing the cardiac benefits reported to date.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics completes acquisition of Mantle Therapeutics
news.summary: Lexeo closed its purchase of Mantle Therapeutics under the merger agreement dated September 16, 2026, making Mantle a wholly owned subsidiary. The deal was announced September 22 together with several new Friedreich ataxia collaborations.

news.headline: Apertura Gene Therapy gives Lexeo access to TfR1 CapX for Friedreich ataxia program
news.summary: Apertura will provide Lexeo access to its TfR1 CapX capsid technology for a program aimed at Friedreich ataxia. It is one of several collaborations announced alongside the Mantle acquisition.

news.headline: Lexeo at Cantor: LX2006 effect well above pivotal powering, PKP2 registrational design still open with FDA
news.summary: Management stressed that LX2006's 28% six-month LVMI reduction in Phase I/II far exceeds the 15% effect size powering SUNRISE-FA 2 (simulations implying ~99% power), with a durable 2.5-3 point mFARS benefit out to two years, and outlined an early commercial build (new MSLs, market-access and cost-offset work, Sf9 process where a handful of batches could supply the US FA market). For LX2020, most HEROIC-PKP2 patients are past six months of follow-up with the 12-month update still slated for later this year, but management conceded the FDA discussion on what NSVT reduction is clinically meaningful and whether a control arm is needed remains unresolved, with registrational-study start pushed to a 2027 goal; shares fell 5.9% to $4.48 that day.

news.headline: 13F season shows Jupiter Topco taking a new 3.95M-share position in Lexeo
news.summary: Jupiter Topco LLC opened a new stake of 3,954,691 shares worth roughly $18.4 million during Q2, while Affinity Asset Advisors held 5.05 million shares, OrbiMed 3.60 million and Dimensional 1.10 million. Institutional investors own about 60.7% of Lexeo.

news.headline: Institutional cluster discloses 5%+ stakes in Lexeo after RMAT and Q2 news
news.summary: Balyasny disclosed 7.84 million shares (9.99% including warrant shares under a blocker), Paradigm BioCapital 5.3%, OrbiMed a combined 5.0% and Affinity Asset Advisors 8.4%, following State Street's 5.5% filing on August 7. The wave of 13Gs around the RMAT designation and Q2 print points to broad specialist accumulation.

news.headline: RBC Capital keeps Outperform on Lexeo, trims price target to $20
news.summary: RBC reiterated Outperform while cutting its target to $20 from $24 after Q2, citing the clean tolerability of Lexeo's AAV cardiac programs. Nine covering analysts sit at an average target of roughly $18.44 (range about $9-$30).

catalysts.label: LX2006 neurologic subscore data at MDS 2026 (Seoul)
catalysts.detail: Oral presentation of new neurological subscore analyses of LX2006 in Friedreich ataxia, including earlier findings of possible early stabilization or improvement versus a matched natural-history cohort.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: Next quarterly results with SUNRISE-FA 2 enrollment and site-activation progress and updated runway commentary against the $234.2 million June cash balance. Based on the August 12 Q2 cadence the print should land in early-to-mid November; the date is not yet confirmed. Any change to the into-2028 runway guidance, or a financing alongside it, would be the key financial signal.

catalysts.label: LX2020 12-month high-dose HEROIC-PKP2 data
catalysts.detail: Twelve-month efficacy and safety update from all high-dose participants in the Phase I/II HEROIC-PKP2 trial in PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, guided for Q4 2026, reaffirmed with Q2 results and again referenced at the September 9 Cantor chat, where management noted most patients are past six months and two nine-month patients showed ~65% NSVT improvement versus ~20% for the cohort. A readout showing durable PKP2 restoration and deepening arrhythmia-burden reduction is needed to answer January's disappointment on protein-to-efficacy correlation. This is the nearest hard datapoint for the stock.

catalysts.label: FDA feedback on LX2020 registrational path
catalysts.detail: With RMAT in hand since August 5, Lexeo is in active FDA discussions on the LX2020 registrational design, specifically what NSVT reduction is clinically meaningful, whether NSVT can serve as a surrogate endpoint and whether a control group is required. Management promised additional clinical and regulatory updates before year-end, while framing finalization of the design and study start as 2027 goals. A single-arm, NSVT-based path would be a major de-risking for a ~60,000-patient US opportunity; a required control arm would lengthen timelines and cost.

catalysts.label: SUNRISE-FA 2 topline data (LX2006)
catalysts.detail: Pivotal open-label readout in Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy comparing roughly 13 high-dose LX2006-treated adults against untreated controls, with LVMI and frataxin expression as FDA-aligned endpoints. The trial is powered on a 15% LVMI effect versus the 28% reduction seen at six months in Phase I/II, which management says implies ~99% probability of detecting the effect. LX2006 holds Breakthrough, RMAT, Orphan and Fast Track designations.

catalysts.label: LX2006 BLA submission (accelerated approval)
catalysts.detail: Targeted BLA under the accelerated-approval pathway based on SUNRISE-FA 2, per the June 2026 FDA alignment, which requires no additional nonclinical bridging and allows use of the commercial-scale Sf9-baculovirus process. Lexeo is already expanding medical affairs and market-access work ahead of it. Submission is contingent on a positive 2H 2027 readout, so this is a target rather than a fixed date.

pulse: Lexeo closed the Mantle Therapeutics acquisition on Sept 29 and added new Friedreich ataxia collaborations (Apertura TfR1 CapX), broadening its FA franchise after the stock slid to ~$3.4 (near its 52-week low of $3.14, down ~23% on the week) following the Sept 9 Cantor chat, where the FDA path for LX2020 stayed unresolved. Near-term markers are the Oct 7 MDS presentation, the Q3 print in November and the Q4 12-month HEROIC-PKP2 data, with SUNRISE-FA 2 topline in 2H 2027 and cash guided into 2028.
